newsitem.title: UK: MSAS expands Manila forwarding operations.
newsitem.headline: MSAS expands Manila forwarding operations.

text.p: MSAS Cargo International said it has expanded its Manila operations into a new office, located next to Ninoy Aquino International airport, doubling the size of the previous facilities.
The global freight forwarder, part of UK-based Ocean Group Plc, said in a statement it had outgrown its previous offices which it had occupied since opening in the Philippines in 1985.

MSAS added that the $350,000 investment moves operations closer to the airport, the 1,300 square-metre offices provide much needed additional space and the move gives the opportunity to invest in upgrading communications systems.

The company said the number of telephone lines had been increased to 40 from 16 and further systems enhancements had positioned the Manila operation ready for the installation of MSAS' global freight tracking and operating system, 'unite121', in August.
MSAS said further Philippines investment was expected this year, with the purchase of additional trucks and a new radio system for its fleet of vehicles and motor cycles.

MSAS said that it was also looking towards establishing a new Manila logistics centre, which would have 3,600 square metres of manufacturing space for value-added services, as well as the facilities for both customs-bonded and non-bonded warehousing.
There is the potential to expand the available space to 10,500 square metres, it added.
Country manager Ole Ringheim said that in the Philippines, MSAS served multi-national companies, mainly in the electronics, semi-conductor and communications industries.

"It is no longer enough for us to just offer transportation services and we are meeting this need by opening our new logistics centre, capable of providing the added-value services our customers demand," he said.
